1.text: In a small village, a farmer named Dara bought a well from his neighbour Malo, for fifty silver coins.

2.text: The next morning, Dara came with his pots. But Malo was already sitting beside the well.

3.text: Malo smiled and said, I sold you the well, Dara. I never sold you the water inside it.

4.text: So every pot you fill, you must pay me rent for my water.

5.text: Dara scratched his head, as the whole village gathered round to watch.

6.text: Then Dara smiled. A slow, dangerous smile.

7.text: You are right, Malo. The water is yours. Every single drop.

8.text: But it is sitting inside my well.

9.text: So from today, you will pay me rent, for storing your water in my well.

10.text: Malo's smile vanished. And the crowd burst out laughing.

11.text: The water's rent was ten coins a month. But the storage rent came to twenty.

12.text: That evening, Malo quietly sold him the water too. For one single coin.

13.text: But tell me. If the water was his all along, why did the clever man end up paying for it twice?
